verdict: UNSURE(the proposal's populations are real, but they are family+weight+size BUCKETS, not bindable populations)
finding: Every 'nodes it absorbs' figure in TYPE-COLOR-SYSTEM.md counts a family+weight+size bucket while IGNORING line-height and letter-spacing, so the number of nodes a new style can actually take WITHOUT changing a visual property is 1.3x to 85x smaller than the figure that justified it.
evidence: Re-measured 2026-09-05, all 5 pages, 20,511 TEXT nodes (census said 20,509; page child counts have also drifted — 1:2 is 81 not 93, 988:2 is 143 not 175). Bound total 8,335 — matches the census exactly, so the two measurements agree on the baseline. Claimed vs family+weight+size bucket vs EXACT recipe match: ui/11 caption medium 1,787 / 1,573 / 21. ui/11 section header 501 / 434 / 0-as-specced. ui/12 small strong 427 / 373 / 5. ui/14 body 322 / 312 / 166. ui/14 panel title strong 634 / 379 / 291. Same pattern for the 6th NEW row the brief did not assign me, ui/12 small medium: claimed 290, Inter-Medium-12 bucket 283, exact 12/18 = 20.
recommend: Quote the exact-match number when justifying a style; quote the bucket number only alongside the line-height change it implies. The two are different decisions — one is free, one is a redesign.

finding: The 1,787-node justification for ui/11 · caption medium is one bucket holding three different treatments; only 21 nodes in the whole file are Inter Medium 11/16 with zero tracking, the value the style must have to sit beside ui/11 · caption.
evidence: Inter Medium 11px bucket = 1,573 nodes (1:3 1,239, 1:4 191, 1:2 79, 1:5 64, 988:2 0). It splits into: 11/16 +8% = 564 (a section header, see D-O-03); 11/16 +0.5px = 521 (also a header — 190/190 on 1:4, 64/64 on 1:5 and 99/255 on 1:3 have all-caps characters); 11/AUTO = 420 on 1:3 alone; 11/15px = 44 on 1:2; 11/16 +0% = 21. Style created at Inter Medium 11 / 16px / 0% — id S:bd306a93111bb1590e430cf2881e9a2055212951.
recommend: Keep the style — it closes a real ramp hole (11 Regular and 13 Medium existed, 11 Medium did not) — but expect it to serve tens, not thousands. The 521 nodes at +0.5px are a SECOND uppercase header treatment competing with the +8% one; pick one tracking value before either is adopted.

screen: ui/11 · section header — created, with two deviations
finding: As specced (Inter Semi Bold, textCase UPPERCASE) this style matches ZERO nodes in the file; the population it was created for is Inter MEDIUM with textCase ORIGINAL, so I built it to the measurement and the deviation is deliberate.
evidence: Inter Semi Bold 11 / 16px / +8% across all 5 pages = 0 nodes. Inter Medium 11 / 16px / +8% = 564 (561 on 1:3, 3 on 1:2). textCase: 0 of 20,511 TEXT nodes on any of the 5 pages use a textCase other than ORIGINAL — uppercase in this file is typed into the characters, never set as a property (558 of the 561 on 1:3 have characters === characters.toUpperCase()). Created as Inter Medium 11 / 16px / 8% / textCase ORIGINAL — id S:2b5b6328c80b96dcd7c0c64f092eab433c7f8c1c, with the reason recorded in the style description.
recommend: If the intent really is Semi Bold and property-level UPPERCASE, that is a redesign of 564 nodes and needs a founder call — it is not adoption. Until then the style as built binds all 564 with no visual change.

screen: ui/12 · small strong — created at 12/18, 201 nodes blocked at 12/16
finding: The 427-node justification is a 12px Semi Bold bucket whose dominant line-height is 16px, not the 18px the proposal specifies — so the style as built is bindable to 5 nodes while 201 sit 2px away from it.
evidence: Inter Semi Bold 12 bucket = 373 (988:2 270, 1:3 93, 1:2 9, 1:5 1). By line-height: 16px = 201 (197 of them on 988:2), AUTO = 93, 14px = 57, 12px = 15, 18px = 5. I built 12/18 (id S:5ee0cb3c3c63bb60e2c1cd116cf8c419f68b3831) because its sibling ui/12 · small is 12/18 and the token is --bk-leading-18; 12/16 is a 988:2-local convention, not a file-wide one — that page also runs Inter Regular 12/16 for 222 more nodes where the ramp says 18.
recommend: Do not quietly rebuild the style at 12/16 to chase the count. Either correct 988:2's 12px line-height to 18 (a 423-node visual change, founder call) or accept that the strong variant serves few nodes today.

screen: Inter Medium 14/20 — 857 nodes, the biggest gap the proposal does not name
verdict: UNSURE(one style value is wrong; correcting it is a visual change to 86 bound nodes)
finding: The largest single unbound exact type combination in the file is Inter Medium 14/20 at 857 nodes, and it misses the existing ui/14 · panel title by exactly 1px of line-height — the style is at 14/21 while DESIGN.md and the code token both say 14/20, so the STYLE is the outlier, not the 857 nodes.
evidence: Inter Medium 14 / 20px / 0% = 857 (988:2 437, 1:3 292, 1:2 109, 1:5 17, 1:4 2), all unbound, 803 of them instance children. Inter Medium 14 / 21px (the style's own value) = 130 nodes total, of which 86 are bound. So the ramp value that is documented in two places serves 130 nodes and the undocumented one serves 857. DESIGN.md:148 says ui/14 · panel title is 14/20; tokens are --bk-text-14 + --bk-leading-20; TYPE-COLOR-SYSTEM.md itself lists this row as a source disagreement but resolves it the other way ('correct DESIGN.md').
recommend: Reverse that resolution: change ui/14 · panel title from 21px to 20px. It is a 1px change to the 86 nodes already bound and it makes 857 nodes bindable with no further edit — the highest-leverage single value in the type system. Founder call because it IS a visual change.

screen: AUTO line-height — the structural ceiling on adoption
verdict: UNSURE(no style can express AUTO; every fix is a visual change)
finding: AUTO line-height, not missing styles, is now the largest single blocker to binding — on 1:3 alone the eleven biggest unbindable populations are all AUTO, totalling 3,110 nodes, and no text style in the file can absorb one without changing its leading.
evidence: 1:3 free-but-no-exact-style = 4,730 nodes; the top 11 combos are Inter Regular 11/AUTO 909, Regular 12/AUTO 559, Regular 13/AUTO 541, Medium 11/AUTO 420, Regular 10/AUTO 392, Medium 12/AUTO 196, Medium 13/AUTO 172, Medium 10/AUTO 160, Semi Bold 13/AUTO 131, Semi Bold 12/AUTO 93, Semi Bold 11/AUTO 82. All 16 styles use PIXELS line-height, so a bind would replace AUTO (Inter's AUTO at 11px is ~13.3px) with 16-32px.
recommend: Adding styles cannot move these. They need a deliberate leading correction per population, which is a redesign decision — and the 392 + 160 nodes at 10px violate the no-size-below-11 rule anyway, so those two are already scheduled changes.

finding: Nothing was bound on a mismatch: every node whose 13 typographic properties did not equal a style's exactly was skipped, including three whole populations that would each have been a silent redesign.
evidence: Skipped by rule: 201 nodes at Inter Semi Bold 12/16 (would have gained 2px of leading from ui/12 · small strong); 857 at Inter Medium 14/20 (would have gained 1px from ui/14 · panel title); every AUTO line-height node (D-O-12); every node with a letterSpacing unit mismatch (a node at 0px vs a style at 0% is visually identical but was still skipped, to keep the rule mechanical). Also skipped: all instance children (1,459 on 988:2, 1,575 on 1:3, 122 on 1:2) — binding those creates overrides rather than fixing the master. setTextStyleIdAsync was available and used throughout; the node.textStyleId assignment fallback was never needed.
recommend: Keep the exact-match rule mechanical. Every population above is a real design decision that deserves its own commit, not a side effect of an adoption pass.
